interfaces.name: Zapier web application
interfaces.technology: Web GUI (Zap editor, dashboard, Tables, Interfaces, Canvas, Agents/Chatbots consoles, and the Platform UI visual integration builder)
interfaces.classification_rationale: Actions are expressed by manipulating presented affordances (views, forms, menus, buttons) of a persistent, navigable representation of account and workflow state. The primitive is affordance manipulation, not command or message.

provenance.evidence: Official help docs describe the Zap editor as a navigable canvas of steps that users configure, test, publish and turn on through on-screen controls. Current.
Official docs describe Platform UI as a visual form editor to build integrations in the browser, confirming a web GUI surface under the same account. Current.

interfaces.name: Zapier Chrome extension
interfaces.classification_rationale: A first-party browser client presenting its own panel where the user selects a Zap, fills fields and clicks Send, then sees results rendered in the panel. Interaction is affordance manipulation on a presented view, so it is Interactive despite the different surface.

provenance.evidence: Official help doc: the extension lets users create, send, retrieve information and run Zap workflows from a toolbar panel with input fields and a Send button. Current.

interfaces.name: Partner API / Workflow API
interfaces.technology: REST API over HTTPS (api.zapier.com, v1/v2, OAuth scopes)
interfaces.classification_rationale: The consumer explicitly invokes provider-defined operations through structured HTTP requests to fixed endpoints (for example POST /v2/action-runs, GET /v2/zap-runs, GET /v1/profiles/me). The primitive is operation invocation under a fixed base and OAuth authentication, so it is one logical interface.

provenance.evidence: Official OpenAPI titled 'Partner API' at base https://api.zapier.com defines discrete operations with OAuth scopes, for example action-runs, action test, zap-runs, accounts. Current.

interfaces.name: Zapier Platform CLI
interfaces.technology: Command-line tool (zapier-platform-cli; commands such as zapier login, deploy, convert)
interfaces.classification_rationale: The consumer explicitly invokes provider-defined commands to build, test, deploy and manage integrations. The primitive is command invocation with no persistent navigable view, so it is Programmatic rather than Interactive. It is a distinct interface from the SDK CLI (different package, deploy-key authentication and purpose).

provenance.evidence: Official docs describe the Platform CLI as a terminal toolset to build, test and manage integrations with commands like zapier convert. Current.

interfaces.name: Zapier SDK CLI
interfaces.technology: Command-line tool (@zapier/zapier-sdk-cli; commands such as list-apps, list-actions, run-action, curl)
interfaces.classification_rationale: The consumer explicitly invokes provider-defined commands from the terminal to inspect and run actions across connected apps. The primitive is command invocation; there is no persistent navigable TUI. It is distinct from the Platform CLI (different package, connection-based authentication and action-execution purpose).

provenance.evidence: Official SDK docs list the CLI commands (list-apps, list-actions, run-action, curl) used to explore and run authenticated actions from the terminal. Current.
Official install router: 'Zapier CLI. Drive Zapier from the terminal', installed via @zapier/zapier-sdk-cli. Current.

interfaces.name: Zapier MCP
interfaces.technology: Model Context Protocol server (hosted at mcp.zapier.com; also a local server via @zapier/zapier-sdk-mcp)
interfaces.classification_rationale: The interface exposes semantically described tools that an MCP client discovers and selects by goal as part of the interaction contract, then invokes. Capability discovery and selection are part of the contract, which is the defining feature of the Agentic paradigm, so it is Agentic rather than Programmatic.

provenance.evidence: Official docs home: one MCP server gives any MCP client governed access to your apps and actions, i.e. discoverable tools selected and invoked by the client. Current.
Official install router: create an MCP server at mcp.zapier.com, add the tools you need, and paste the server URL into the client's MCP settings. Current.

interfaces.name: Zapier Copilot (natural-language assistant)
interfaces.technology: In-product AI assistant chat (Copilot in the Zap editor, home page and Agents; the Agents natural-language chat surface shares this paradigm)
interfaces.classification_rationale: The consumer expresses intent through natural-language messages that the service interprets to build and edit Zaps, agents, tables, interfaces and actions. The primitive is the message and tool orchestration is internal to the service, so it is Conversational rather than Agentic.

provenance.evidence: Official help doc: Copilot is an AI assistant you chat with in a prompt box; you describe the workflow and it creates, configures and refines the Zap. Current (open beta).
Official help doc: you instruct and refine Agents through a natural-language chat field, confirming a message-primitive surface. Current.

access_mechanism_ledger.mechanism: Web application (Zap editor, dashboard, Tables, Interfaces, Canvas, Platform UI visual builder)

access_mechanism_ledger.detail: No first-party consumer mobile app. Zapier tested an iOS beta in 2020 that was never released; the only store apps are internal event apps.
No native desktop application. The browser-based client is the Chrome extension, already counted.

access_mechanism_ledger.mechanism: Terminal / CLI TUI (surface check for each CLI)
access_mechanism_ledger.detail: Neither the Platform CLI nor the SDK CLI exposes a persistent navigable TUI dashboard; both are command interfaces, counted as Programmatic.
Client library that wraps Zapier's API and materializes as the SDK CLI and a local MCP server; SDKs are not counted as logical interfaces.
Folded into the Conversational interface: the agent chat shares the natural-language-message primitive with Copilot (same channel).
A customer-facing chatbot product that users build and embed for their own end-users; it is an output artifact, not an interface for accessing the Zapier platform.

access_mechanism_ledger.mechanism: Webhooks by Zapier / Email by Zapier (inbound catch hooks and email triggers)
access_mechanism_ledger.detail: Built-in trigger apps configured inside a Zap, not a standalone provider-wide access interface.
Deprecated and no longer developed or supported; officially superseded by Zapier MCP.

access_mechanism_ledger.mechanism: Powered by Zapier / Embed / White Label
access_mechanism_ledger.detail: A distribution of existing interfaces (the Partner/Workflow API plus the embedded web Zap editor), not a new logical interface.

access_mechanism_ledger.mechanism: SDKs, client libraries, OAuth, API keys, npm packages, App Directory
access_mechanism_ledger.detail: Support or implement interfaces but are not themselves logical interfaces per the counting rules.
